name: Navigation and shared frame
critique: The App Sidebar gives the area a clear frame. However, its session-history section appears only in the instruction/detail view. That view highlights Activities while its title says Workspace intelligence and its tab names a session. The workspace name is routinely truncated. Lifecycle styles still target .wi-lifecycle, which the new IntelligenceShell no longer mounts; rounded cards and inconsistent sizing have reappeared.
impact: Navigation changes shape as the user moves through one task, and the visual system varies between destinations.
target: Keep the licensed sidebar. Use a stable work navigation, meaningful page titles and breadcrumbs, and one documented style adapter. Move session history out of the global rail. Restore the intended styles through the actual shell scope, rather than adding more unrelated overrides.
components: AppSidebar, ChatLayout, shared FullscreenWorkbench, official Untitled UI controls
acceptance: Every destination has a clear selected item and title; collapse and mobile overlay remain usable; no orphaned host selectors; 15–16px body text and readable secondary labels.

name: Overview before setup
critique: The new landing provides orientation, but an oversized Plan Overview card dominates. Static onboarding steps are presented as To-dos with a download action. Knowledge inventory is shown without explaining its relationship to agent access; only eight of ten records are listed. Recent work is pushed down the page.
impact: The screen looks like an approval plan and can make inventory look like authorized context.
target: Use a compact setup/readiness summary with one setup action. Show purpose as not established, readiness blockers, knowledge coverage and work needing attention. Label inventory separately from knowledge authorized for the agent; make omitted records discoverable.
components: AgentSummary or compact AgentGate composition, KnowledgeSources, RunLog
acceptance: At normal desktop height, readiness and recent/actionable work are visible together; the setup CTA is clear; static steps are not implied to be running work.

name: Overview after activation
entry: Overview when a coordinator binding exists
critique: The activated branch substitutes an AgentSummary and a pending-suggestion notice. It does not organize purpose, accepted knowledge coverage, gaps, automatic-review state and activities requiring action into a coherent operational overview.
impact: An activated workspace still lacks a clear answer to what its agent understands and what the user should address next.
target: Give the overview a stable structure across setup and active states: purpose and readiness, needs attention, coverage, recent outcomes. Distinguish agent publication, enabled policy and actual running work.
components: AgentSummary, KnowledgeSources, RunLog, ThinkingState only for actual work
acceptance: Published, enabled, paused, queued and waiting-for-review are distinct; coverage and gaps reflect accepted data; unavailable metrics stay absent.

name: Activities list
critique: The list is mainly goal text, state and time. It has no task-oriented search or filters for needs-answer, review, failure, executor or affected artifact. A repeated setup notice competes with the history. Completed labels do not summarize outcomes or modifications.
impact: Users cannot quickly find the work that needs them or understand what changed.
target: Make Activities a work inbox with status filters, search, executor, target and concise outcome. Keep runtime status separate from result, such as answered, draft proposed or changes saved. Do not infer workspace modifications from completion alone.
components: RunLog adapted to real fields, official search/filter controls
acceptance: User can find waiting work, open the exact activity and return to preserved list filters; all labels have a consistent status mapping.

name: New instruction
critique: This opens a blank conversation draft, New session tab, starter prompts and composer. Clicking it alone does not enqueue work; sending creates a session if needed and submits a goal. The screen does not identify an executor or make scope and expected outcome explicit. Read only is a starter label, not an independently visible execution contract.
impact: The user cannot tell whether they are opening a chat, assigning an agent or requesting a workspace change.
target: Replace the product concept with New activity. Present a work brief: goal, named executor/default workspace agent, selected evidence, expected outcome and permitted mode. Natural-language entry remains available inside that composition. Derive readiness and capabilities from policy; do not silently switch legacy sessions to another executor.
components: StarterPrompts, PromptInput/ChatComposer, KnowledgeSources, AttachmentsTray, existing agent selection controls
acceptance: The draft clearly identifies who will act and what evidence is included; submission creates one activity with a receipt; cancelling an untouched draft causes no model call.
source: components/intelligence/workspace.tsx newSession, send, empty and composer branches

name: Activity detail and completed result
critique: A selected work item is still presented under a session title such as explain this workspace. The actual goal is only a message in the transcript. The completed sample asks an A/B/C/D question in prose, while the activity is marked Completed. A persistent composer does not distinguish answering a pending interaction from starting follow-up work.
impact: The identity and outcome of the activity are difficult to understand; a question can look actionable without any structured pending interaction.
target: Use the activity goal as the title, with executor, status, target and outcome summary. Separate result, decisions and execution detail. Keep the transcript as supporting history. Distinguish Reply to a recorded question from Create follow-up activity. Do not retroactively fabricate pending forms from historical prose.
components: ThreadHeader, ChatThread/ChatScreen as supporting content, ArtifactPanel, AgentGate
acceptance: Opening any historical row shows its own goal and receipts; state and next action agree; history stays readable without confusing a new request with a resume.

name: Queued and working activity
entry: Goal accepted, queued, preparing, reasoning, tool execution or delegated work
critique: The principal status indicator is an inline ThinkingState near the end of the transcript. It can be below the visible content. Generic Thinking or Running a tool gives little task context; stopping work shares the composer area.
impact: Users must hunt for confirmation that work started and what is happening now.
target: Keep a compact persistent activity status near the title, an inline current-operation summary and a visible Stop control while active. Link to the execution pane. Use actual receipts for operation names and elapsed time; keep queue admission separate from execution.
components: ThinkingState, ThreadHeader, AgentRunTree, official icon controls
acceptance: Queued, running, waiting and reconnecting remain visible while scrolling; acknowledgement appears immediately; Stop has a clear pending and terminal state.

name: Clarification and answer submission
critique: Actual structured interactions render through GenerativeForm with Continue, but the sampled completed activity contains an unstructured A/B/C/D question and no form. Generated forms share the same narrow label presentation as the agent editor. Continuation feedback is separated from the question.
impact: Users cannot reliably tell which questions need an answer or whether an answer resumed work.
target: Require question-producing tools to emit the existing structured interaction contract. Give questions a clear Awaiting your answer state. Keep validation, submitting, answer accepted and resumed feedback with the form. Use Answer and continue when it resumes an activity. Preserve historical prose as historical content.
components: GenerativeForm, ThinkingState, existing structured question adapter
acceptance: Each live question has accessible controls and one submission path; accepted answers become a read-only decision record; prose alone never creates a fake resumable interaction.
source: components/intelligence/workspace.tsx interaction, answer and pendingHere branches

name: Saved context selector
critique: The pane stacks an Attached context card with a separate Choose saved revisions form. Ten resources appear as a flat checkbox list; names, type and revision occupy one label. No search or grouping is available. The ten-item attachment limit appears only through validation.
impact: Large workspaces will be hard to navigate, and selecting evidence is detached from the work brief.
target: Use one context-selection panel: searchable typed inventory, selected count, revision details and an explicit limit. Explain next-activity context separately from session uploads and agent-authorized knowledge.
components: KnowledgeSources, GenerativeForm where suitable, ContextWindow, official search/filter controls
acceptance: Resources can be found by name/type; full names and revisions are readable; selection survives validation; the user can distinguish selected evidence from authorized scope.

name: Uploads and attachments
entry: Upload files and attachment tray in instruction view
critique: Saved context and file upload are now different labeled controls, which is an improvement. However, the upload policy paragraph stays prominent on the empty screen, and the relationship between a persisted Source and its attachment to the next activity is not obvious. Uploads are limited to text/Markdown, 250 KB each.
impact: Users may mistake a local attachment action for a temporary file or expect broader ingestion support.
target: Place Saved knowledge and Upload file in one Attach action with distinct choices. Keep the attachment tray next to the work brief; show persistence and upload restrictions at selection time. Surface progress, retry and detach without implying detach deletes the Source.
components: AttachmentsTray, KnowledgeSources, official menu and upload controls
acceptance: Owners/admins and permitted editors can upload; viewers cannot; saved Source creation and attachment state are independently legible; unsupported types show useful errors.
source: components/intelligence/workspace.tsx upload handlers and composer; lib/agent/context-uploads.ts

name: Session history and archive management
entry: Active/Archived session section in activity detail
critique: Session history is nested under primary workspace navigation and appears only in the workbench. A session title can cover multiple distinct activities. Archive/delete belong to that session while users are browsing individual work items. The distinction between closing a tab, archiving history and deleting history is easy to miss.
impact: Users can lose their place or misunderstand the scope of a history action.
target: Keep activity navigation primary. Place related sessions in a clearly named secondary history view or contextual section. Explain archive as hiding history and delete eligibility as no workspace modifications. Preserve the backend modification-based deletion guard.
components: SessionList, SessionTabs only where useful, official contextual menus
acceptance: Close, archive, restore and delete have distinct wording and scope; ineligible deletion explains why; archive never implies cancellation or rollback.
source: components/intelligence/workspace.tsx history, changeSession and archived state

name: Session runs panel
critique: The panel is titled Session runs and duplicates the global Activities list. Duration and cost columns are still mounted without supplied telemetry. Selecting a row opens another Activity pane while the main transcript can remain on a different work item.
impact: Two selections can refer to different activities without a clear relationship.
target: Rename this Related activities if retained. Show only real columns. Make selecting a related activity update the canonical activity view, or explicitly label it as comparing another run.
components: RunLog, PanelDock, ThreadHeader
acceptance: No empty telemetry columns; selected activity identity is visible in both content and inspector; the list states its session scope.

name: Run tree and trace viewer
critique: The pane combines status, recorded tokens, a run tree and detailed timing in a narrow column. The inspected run is Completed while an earlier tool call is highlighted as failed. The failure detail says only The call failed, with richer receipts elsewhere.
impact: A recoverable call error can look like the whole activity failed; diagnosis requires switching between representations.
target: Use execution summary first, expandable run tree second and trace on demand. Show whether errors were recovered and link to the exact tool receipt. Use an expandable full-width diagnostic mode for dense traces.
components: AgentRunTree, TraceViewer, ThreadHeader, PanelDock
acceptance: Terminal activity status and child-call outcomes are distinguished; failed call details lead to input/output/error receipts; missing timing is stated rather than invented.

name: Raw run logs
entry: Run logs disclosure in Activity pane
critique: Logs are nested native details elements with timestamps, summaries and JSON. This is an appropriate place for raw receipts, but the current log presentation lacks filtering, correlation with selected spans and a clear business/diagnostic boundary.
impact: Operators must manually reconcile a tool call with the error or result that caused it.
target: Keep raw results available in a Logs/Receipts diagnostic subview. Add event-type filtering, search, copy and selected-call correlation using a licensed log presentation if available; retain the existing receipt contract.
components: TraceViewer and licensed log component after source inspection; existing raw receipt adapter
acceptance: Raw JSON stays in diagnostics; selecting a call opens its receipt; errors preserve call ID/time and redact credentials under existing backend rules.

name: Ontology proposal review
entry: Review changes on an ontology proposal
critique: ArtifactPanel switches between Markdown documents for saved and proposed versions, followed by a large plan approval card. Entity/relationship names and removed items are listed, but property-level changes and graph impact are not the central review object.
impact: Users cannot confidently assess a large ontology change from counts and prose alone.
target: Build a change-review composition around summary, structured additions/changes/removals, evidence and a read-only ontology preview. Keep raw definitions secondary. Preserve baseline-version conflict checks and explicit draft application.
components: ArtifactPanel, AgentGate, KnowledgeSources, existing ontology renderer in read-only review mode
acceptance: Property-level and removal effects are reviewable before apply; stale baseline blocks apply visibly; success links to the actual saved draft revision.

name: Process proposal review
entry: Review changes on a process proposal
critique: The proposed process is rendered as a Markdown element list and complete JSON definition, while the saved process is JSON. There is no process-map review in the intelligence pane.
impact: The user is asked to approve a visual process by reading its serialized structure.
target: Use the existing process renderer for a read-only before/after or change overlay, with lanes, routes and agent activities visible. Keep semantic changes and execution implications beside the map. Raw JSON remains a secondary diagnostic option.
components: ArtifactPanel, AgentGate, existing process renderer and diagram adapter
acceptance: Routing, lane assignment and agent activities are reviewable before applying; applying remains draft-only and does not imply compilation, publication or execution.

name: Suggestions list and empty state
coverage: Browser empty state plus source populated state
critique: The empty state is one sentence telling the user to activate and give an inspection goal, with no direct next step. Populated suggestions are a long vertical stack of cards with rationale, another plan card, state text and knowledge lists; there is no triage/filter structure.
impact: Before setup the screen is a dead end; after setup it can become an unscannable review queue.
target: Make Suggestions a triage list with pending/accepted/dismissed states, purpose, executor, evidence confidence and target. Explain the exact readiness blocker in an empty state and link to its resolution. Open detailed acceptance in a focused review.
components: RunLog/list composition, AgentGate, KnowledgeSources, official filter controls
acceptance: No-setup, no-suggestions and load-error are different; pending work is filterable; accepted suggestions link to resulting activities.

name: Suggested assignment acceptance
critique: The same goal and rationale are repeated above and inside AgentGate. Executor can be missing, which disables approval with a specialist-must-be-published explanation. Context is mainly a count until a separate knowledge card is read; the resulting action is called Accept assignment.
impact: Users cannot easily judge who will act, on which resources, and why the assignment is safe to start.
target: Show one assignment brief: goal, executor revision, context, success criteria, permitted capabilities and rationale. Make readiness failures resolvable. Label acceptance with its consequence, such as Accept and start activity, when that is what the backend dispatches.
components: AgentGate, AgentSummary, KnowledgeSources
acceptance: Executor and pinned context are visible before acceptance; missing executor has a clear resolution; acceptance produces one linked activity with an acknowledgement.

name: Agents list
critique: The screen uses a card-style list beside a detail area that initially contains a single instruction. The list repeats Agents and draft counts, while row names/descriptions truncate. New specialist is the creation action even though the list also includes a coordinator.
impact: Users need to infer the distinction between the workspace agent and specialists.
target: Keep a clear roster with role, responsibility, publication/enabled state and recent outcome. Distinguish the workspace coordinator from specialists visually and semantically. Select a record deliberately without leaving a large unexplained empty detail region.
components: AgentList, AgentSummary, official search/filter controls
acceptance: Coordinator and specialists are distinguishable; complete responsibilities remain discoverable; draft/published/paused/archived states are consistent.

name: Create specialist
critique: AgentCreate asks for a description and offers Create draft, plus a separate full-width Create a manual draft button. The surrounding roster stays in place. The draft preview surface exposes little about model, scope or limits before generation, and readiness failures are not presented as a concise checklist.
impact: Two creation paths feel unrelated and the expected result of generation is unclear.
target: Use one specialist creation flow with Generate from responsibility and Configure manually as clear entry modes. Explain that generation produces a draft with no granted knowledge access; review remains required. Display provider readiness before generation.
components: AgentCreate, AgentSummary, GenerativeForm
acceptance: Generated and manual drafts converge on the same editor; creating a draft does not publish or enable it; cancellation and generation failure retain entered responsibility.

name: Agent detail
critique: AgentSummary is followed by detached Edit/Archive buttons and then another large publication card. Edit draft appears twice. Model display says Workspace MiniMax rather than identifying the configured binding; some record actions live in the list overflow as well.
impact: Record identity, lifecycle actions and configuration are fragmented across the page.
target: Compose one agent record header with responsibility, role, publication/enabled state and primary action. Put configuration, authorized knowledge and recent activities in clear sections; keep destructive actions in one contextual menu.
components: AgentSummary, AgentList, AgentGate, official contextual menu
acceptance: Each action has one primary location; publication and enablement are separate; latest activity opens the exact work item rather than an ambiguous session.

name: Agent draft editor
critique: Visible labels truncate to Maximum reaso…, Result JSON Sc… and Use the latest sa…. Instructions, runtime limits, output schema, tool permissions and knowledge resources form one long sequence. The result schema is shown even in the sampled interactive mode. Save/Discard are at the end of the form.
impact: Important permissions and limits are difficult to read or review, and actions are far from the current field.
target: Recompose the form into Responsibility, Tools, Knowledge and Advanced runtime sections using licensed fields and official controls. Use full-width labels above controls, conditional schema editing and a persistent save/discard area. Explain future-revision behavior in the knowledge section.
components: GenerativeForm with appropriate layout adaptation, KnowledgeSources, official form controls, code editor for schema
acceptance: No label truncation at desktop or narrow widths; permitted tools and evidence are grouped; all changes and validation errors remain visible before save.

name: Publish, pause and archive agent
coverage: Browser publication view plus source mutations
critique: Publishing is presented as a large To-dos plan listing raw tool IDs. Pause/resume is a summary switch, while archive inserts another gate. The current presentation makes lifecycle consequences less clear than the underlying contracts.
impact: A user may confuse publication, permission changes, execution availability and removal from the roster.
target: Use a focused publication review with a capability/scope change summary, immutable revision identity and explicit post-publish enabled state. Explain pause as preventing new assignments; archive as record lifecycle, without implying cancellation of existing work.
components: AgentGate, AgentSummary, official confirmation dialog/menu
acceptance: Publish, enable, pause and archive state transitions are independently explained; role restrictions and in-flight work consequences are shown; raw tool names have human labels.

name: Workspace setup input
critique: A purpose text area is followed by a flat resource checkbox list. Purpose, selection and Inspect selected knowledge share a generic generated-form layout; the steps from ingesting evidence to activating a coordinator are not clearly represented. Non-managers do not get an equally useful read-only setup summary.
impact: Workspace setup feels like a form submission rather than establishing the workspace agent’s operating context.
target: Use a staged setup composition: Purpose → Knowledge → Inspect → Review → Activate. Make evidence selection searchable and revisions clear. Keep administrator actions separate from the read-only workspace understanding view.
components: GenerativeForm, KnowledgeSources, ContextWindow, AgentGate
acceptance: Users know which step they are on and what inspection sends to the model; permissions are clear; a source count is not mistaken for inspected coverage.

name: Workspace inspection progress and setup history
entry: Setup inspection queued/running or previous setup selected
critique: Prior setups appear as buttons named Activated setup, Review setup or a status, without meaningful identity. Current inspection uses inline ThinkingState and an Open setup activity link. The setup form and previous history remain in the same long page.
impact: Users cannot clearly identify an inspection, compare attempts or follow evidence coverage.
target: Create an inspection record view with objective, selected revisions, current stage, coverage and gaps. Make previous inspections a dated history with outcome summaries. Link its execution trace without forcing the user into a conversation to understand progress.
components: ThinkingState, AgentRunTree, RunLog, KnowledgeSources
acceptance: Every setup attempt has an identifiable purpose/time/state; queued and rejected requests differ; partial/failed coverage and next actions are explicit.
source: components/intelligence/agent-lifecycle.tsx setups list, polling and setup.work branches

name: Setup configuration review and activation
critique: ArtifactPanel shows a Markdown report including the full JSON definition. Separate editable fields, individual gap checkboxes, an initial-inspection checkbox and a final AgentGate are stacked below. Start initial inspection is true by default.
impact: An important authority and evidence decision is spread over several representations; activation can also immediately start work.
target: Provide one review with purpose/goals, coverage, unresolved gaps, executor capabilities and operating limits. Summarize configuration changes structurally; put raw JSON in advanced details. Make Activate only versus Activate and inspect an explicit reviewed consequence, preserving existing contracts.
components: ArtifactPanel, AgentGate, KnowledgeSources, GenerativeForm, official controls
acceptance: All accepted gaps and grants are visible together; incomplete coverage cannot look complete; activation consequence and any initial work are unambiguous.

name: Automatic knowledge review
entry: Select the bound coordinator as manager
critique: The Automatic knowledge review form is inserted before AgentSummary and includes per-day run/token controls. It is discoverable only by selecting the coordinator. Policy elsewhere mentions preserved ambient triggers without exposing this relationship.
impact: The ambient behavior central to the product is hidden inside an agent record and can be confused with global enablement.
target: Give the workspace agent a visible Automation section with trigger, authorized knowledge, limits, pending changes and last review outcome. Link it from Overview and Workspace policy. Keep opt-in admission limits and accepted coordinator revision explicit.
components: AgentSummary, GenerativeForm, RunLog, KnowledgeSources
acceptance: Users can discover whether automatic review is on, what triggers it, its budget and what is pending; enabling a rule does not imply automatic acceptance of suggestions.

name: Workspace policy
critique: The dialog is titled Agent settings. It combines Enable workspace agent, working mode, Allow MiniMax assistance and connection revision. Even with the saved enabled/Assist/allowed configuration loaded, it says Assistance will be enabled when you save. Runtime options, budgets and triggers are described as preserved but not explained here.
impact: This is the exact readiness control users previously struggled to find; the dialog still does not clearly distinguish saved state from edited state.
target: Use a consistently named Workspace policy surface with a current readiness summary and separate Provider access, Execution mode and Automation links. Explain dependencies and show saved versus unsaved values. Identify the configured connection without exposing credentials.
components: Official Untitled UI modal/form controls, GenerativeForm where suitable, AgentSummary readiness
acceptance: Saved policy state is truthful; users can identify the blocker to execution; absent/revoked/stale connections have actionable guidance; no save is implied necessary when nothing changed.

name: Errors, access restrictions and disconnected states
coverage: Source only except sampled terminal trace
critique: Errors surface through several paragraphs, form errors and diagnostic panels. Uncertain, suspended, budget exhausted, loading, reconnecting and forbidden conditions are not composed into one consistent recovery model. State labels also lose detail when reduced to chat ready/streaming/error states.
impact: Users cannot reliably tell whether to answer, review, reconnect, change access, create follow-up work or stop.
target: Design a common state contract with inline field errors, persistent activity outcome, connection state and contextual recovery actions. Keep uncertain outcomes conservative: inspect receipts first, never blindly retry a potentially completed mutation. Provide useful viewer/editor/admin read-only presentations.
components: ThinkingState, AgentGate, official alerts and dialogs, RunLog
acceptance: Every backend state has a visible meaning and permitted next action; stale proposals block apply; revoked roles disable writes; reconnecting never looks like new execution.
